# Grok Build session fixtures

These reduced files target **Grok Build 1.0.52**, checked locally in a scratch `GROK_HOME`. They keep the fields cornercase reads and drop everything else. Paths are `/home/user/...`. Session ids, account ids and request ids are replaced. `summary.json` has no `agent_id` and no `attempt_id`. Nothing here is a credential, and cornercase never reads `auth.json`.

A pane is the row in `active_sessions.json` whose `pid` is the foreground process. On Linux that row's `pid_start` has to match field 22 of `/proc/<pid>/stat` (clock ticks since boot). A missing start time, which is what macOS returns, does not reject the row. The session directory is `sessions/<percent-encoded cwd>/<id>/`, with uppercase hex and the RFC 3986 unreserved characters left as they are. When that name would be longer than a file name, Grok writes a short directory plus a sibling `.cwd` file holding the path; cornercase finds the id and checks `.cwd` or `summary.json`'s `info.cwd` instead of rebuilding the hash.

`events.jsonl` `turn_ended` ends a turn (`completed` or `cancelled`). `turn_completed` in `updates.jsonl` is the usage record, not the end of the turn. Waiting is a `permission_prompt` phase, a `permission_requested` with no later `permission_resolved`, or an open `ask_user_question` or `exit_plan_mode` while the turn is open. Other tools, including a foreground or background shell, stay working. A title containing `Action Required` means waiting only while the turn is open. A braille spinner, and the word Waiting in a compact title, do not.

The context percentage is one model call's `inputTokens` over `signals.json` `contextWindowTokens` (else `summary.json` `context_window`), rounded and capped. A summed multi-call `inputTokens`, a changed `current_model_id`, or a newer `auto_compact_completed` / `compaction_checkpoint` leaves the model with no percentage. `contextWindowUsage`, `compactionCount` and `_meta.totalTokens` are not the figure. Stats take `inputTokens - cachedReadTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cachedReadTokens` and `cacheCreationTokens`, and do not add `reasoningTokens` again. Prompts are chat lines with `prompt_index` and no `synthetic_reason`. A `session_relationship` other than `primary` adds tokens only.

`/ ` and `!` are local commands. `?` is a real prompt. There is no plan-usage probe. Resume is `grok <args> --resume <summary info.id>`.
